Chris Lavan, Associate Vice Provost, ATL, JCODL Chair Purpose of the Committee The purpose of the Joint Committee on Online and Distance Learning (JCODL) is to propose, examine, and recommend institutional policies and practices for developing, planning, and evaluating online and distance learning with a focus on quality, sustainability, and connection to the University’s mission, with approval of the Faculty Senate and Provost.
Further, JCODL, considers faculty training, quality in delivery of online offerings, student learning outcomes, and ADA compliance regarding online and distance learning, as well as develops and implements strategic plans for online courses, certificate, and degree programs. (University Manual 5.78.10 - 5.78.11).
Executive Summary The committee discussed several topics internally (listed in the next section) during the 2024-2025 academic year, and brought forth one proposal for consideration and a vote to the university’s Faculty Senate.

Proposal: Updated Adoption of New Course Modalities and Methods of Instruction This proposal had been a priority of this committee for three academic years, and with collaboration between several Faculty Senators, including past Curriculum and Standards 1

Committee (CASC) Chair and Faculty Senate Executive Committee (FSEC) member Senator Preisser, as well as the Office of the Provost and University Registrar’s Office, the proposal was introduced during the November 2024 Faculty Senate meeting.
At the November Faculty Senate meeting the proposal was tabled, but then brought back to the floor of the Faculty Senate during its January 2025 meeting where it was approved by a vote during that same meeting.
Ultimately, the initial proposal for updated recognized teaching methods evolved to include methods of instruction as well.
